purpose: PC lab target: x86-64, UEFI (OVMF), QEMU q35, single vCPU. Single-image Rust kernel (kernel/, x86_64-unknown-uefi) per ADR-0001/ADR-0002.

disk.note: 64 MiB raw FAT32 image made by tools/fat32.py for every run (lab files + raw pattern in the last 8 sectors); a multi-phase case keeps it between its phases

boot_oracle.oracle: contracts/boot.md v1: boot|start, boot|ebs|ok=1, then kernel|post_ebs with map_key and descriptors emitted from kernel/ after ExitBootServices; QEMU exit 33 (0x10 via isa-debug-exit); no boot|error

M1.oracle: contracts/boot.md v1 success path (see boot_oracle); kernel-owned page tables active (vmm line: WP, NXE, section permissions, direct map), guarded stack adopted; scheduler self-check (kernel thread spawned and joined, no frame left) and ring-3 ping as process 1; object self-check (VMO through a kernel channel, peer close seen, nothing left); ELF loader self-check (embedded hello app exits 7 after trace+ping, no frame left); PCI enumerated through the MCFG ECAM window; virtio-blk self-check (modern device 0x1042, VERSION_1+FLUSH, sector 0 read, flush); FAT32 volume mounted and /HELLO.TXT read; WP-24: the service manager starts from the volume as the first process with a control channel and answers `OK 0` to the lab manifest (kernel|svcmgr|…|reply=OK 0|code=ok|selfcheck=1|wait_ticks=…)

contracts/boot.md v1 failure path: stale map key injected -> firmware rejects EBS twice -> boot|error|code=BOOT_E_EBS_FAILED, boot|halt|reboot=0, QEMU exit 97 (0x30); exactly one boot|start (no reboot loop); kernel never entered

M2.oracle: SDM Table 7-1: #DE vector 0, no error code (fault: RIP at div); lab exit 145
#UD vector 6, fault at ud2; exit 157
#DB single-step trap: saved RIP after the nop (SDM Event 1); exit 147
#GP on non-canonical address, error code 0 (SDM Event 13); exit 171
#PF write to unmapped supervisor page: error code 2, CR2 = target (SDM Fig. 7-11); exit 173
#BP is a trap: handler prints and returns; saved RIP after int3 (SDM Event 3)
iretq path restores 15 GPRs and CF/DF
corrupt RSP -> #PF undeliverable -> #DF (SDM Table 7-5) on IST1 stack, error code 0; exit 161
fault inside handler stops at nesting limit 3 with a fixed message; exit 157

sidt-based walk: 0..=31 present interrupt gates to stubs pushing the vector (dummy 0 where the CPU pushes no error code); 32..=255 present interrupt gates to the uniform interrupt entries (push 0, push imm32 vector); exit 33
empty IDT + fault = triple fault -> QEMU reset -> exit 0 under -no-reboot; proves the runner detects a reset (no exception line printed)
1024 distinct, aligned, >=1 MiB, writable frames; counters move by N and return after free

stress/limit/recovery: alloc until None (count == free_frames, free_frames == 0 after, further alloc None, no panic); every frame given back through an intrusive list; counters back to the start and a new allocation succeeds
required_markers: |ktest|pass|exhaustion returns None without panic and the allocator recovers fully

M2.oracle: free twice -> NotAllocated; <1MiB, misaligned, bitmap storage -> Unmanaged

after the CR3 switch: CR3 = kernel PML4, CR0.WP and EFER.NXE set, .text RX / .data RW+NX / headers R+NX, direct map aliases RAM, null page and stack guard pages unmapped, boot-services memory reclaimed, allocator still works; exit 33

firmware-independent: WP cleared -> supervisor write to the read-only header page goes through (restored); kernel's enable_wp -> write to .text raises #PF error code 3 (present, write, supervisor: SDM Fig. 7-11), CR2 = RIP = target; exit 173
instruction fetch from .data under EFER.NXE -> #PF error code 0x11 (present, instruction fetch: SDM Fig. 7-11 bit 4); CR2 = RIP = target; exit 173
push loop overflows the guarded kernel stack: #PF in the guard page cannot push its frame -> #DF (SDM Table 7-5) on the guarded IST1 stack, error code 0, CR2 = stack base - 8; exit 161
periodic LAPIC timer at 1000 Hz (PIT-calibrated): two PIT-measured 50 ms windows each deliver 25..=100 ticks, monotonic, no unexpected vector, max handler depth 1, IF clear after disable; exit 33
self-IPI on vector 0x41 delivered and handled; after EOI a second IPI on the same vector is delivered (without EOI the ISR bit would hold it); no unexpected vector; max handler depth 1; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|EOI acknowledged, next interrupt delivered, no re-entry

M2.oracle: software int 0xFF (spurious: counted, no EOI), int 0x20 (masked PIC vector) and int 0xF0 (unassigned) are counted as unexpected and return; with the timer stopped and interrupts enabled for 20 ms nothing arrives; SVR = 0x1FF; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|spurious and masked vectors are counted, never fault

M2.oracle: irqsave lock: IF cleared inside and restored after (from enabled and from disabled); the periodic timer delivers no tick while the lock is held for 20 ms and resumes after release; try_lock fails while held and succeeds when free; protected value updated; exit 33
re-acquiring a held IrqSpinLock on the same CPU panics with K_E_LOCK_REENTRY|lock=ktest_lock instead of hanging; exit 35
explicit panic! prints OSX|<build>|kernel|panic|loc=kernel/src/ktest.rs:<line>:<col>|console_was_locked=0|msg=<message> and exits 0x11 (QEMU 35)

M3.oracle: 10,000 mixed allocations/frees (70% <= 2 KiB, 25% <= 16 KiB, 5% <= 196 KiB) with content checks; afterwards live_blocks, slab_pages, large_frames and PMM free frames equal their values before the stress (the scheduler owns live blocks since WP-15); exit 33

frame mapped at the scratch page, written through it and read back through the direct map; unmap returns the frame and flushes the TLB; a write then raises #PF error code 2 with CR2 = RIP target = the page; exit 173
scratch page made read-only (protect + invlpg): content readable, a write raises #PF error code 3 with CR2 = the page; exit 173

user space with three USER pages (invisible from the kernel space); while active the kernel reads a value written through the direct map and writes one back; after return the write is visible; destroy frees everything (frame count equal); mappings outside USER_BASE..USER_END refused; exit 33
ring-3 ping program exits 0x1235 through SYS_EXIT; ring-3 trace program copies 'hello from r3' through validated user memory (user|trace line) and exits 13; no frame leaked; exit 33

SYS_TRACE with an unmapped user pointer returns ERR_FAULT and with a kernel pointer ERR_RANGE; the program exits 0xfdfc and the kernel continues; exit 33 (the boot self-check's hello app traces len=14 earlier in the log; only a len=8 trace would betray a bad-pointer copy)

ring-3 read of the kernel direct map -> #PF taken in ring 3 (error code 0x5: present, user), diagnosed as kernel|user_fault|vector=14 and the run ends with exit code 0x1000e; the kernel continues (test exit 33)

two processes run the same program at the same virtual addresses concurrently: each reads 0 from its fresh data page, writes a pattern, sleeps 20 ticks while the other runs, and still finds its own pattern (exit code 1<<63 for both: first read 0, pattern kept); no process record and no frame remains; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|two processes at the same virtual addresses are isolated

M3.oracle: SYS_CHECK_RIP with a non-canonical address is refused with ERR_RANGE (program exits 0xfffffffffffffffc); no #GP in ring 0; exit 33

two kernel threads of priority 0 yield to each other: log ABABABABABABABAB (16 entries), join returns 'A'/'B', a third thread sleeps 5 ticks and measures 5..=50, switches >= 18, free frames equal before/after (after a warm-up thread); exit 33

a spinning kernel thread (priority 1, never yields) and the boot thread (never yields, halts between ticks) alternate under the timer: >= 3 handovers observed, preemptions >= 2 x handovers, spinner exits with its count, max handler depth 1, no unexpected vector; exit 33

fixed priorities are honoured across a quantum boundary: a priority-0 thread runs 15 ticks (> QUANTUM_TICKS 10) without yielding and a priority-3 spinner never advances meanwhile (spinner_advanced_during_high=0); once the driver sleeps the spinner runs (spinner_ran_after=1); frames balance; exit 33

after a warm-up process and thread: a process exiting through SYS_EXIT (0x1235), one ended by a ring-3 #PF (0x1000e) and a kernel thread (join 7) leave PMM free frames, heap live blocks, slab pages, thread count (1) and process count (0) exactly as before; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|process and thread exit return every frame

M3.oracle: ring-3 program calls SYS_SLEEP(3) then SYS_YIELD (ABI v1.1), both return 0, exits 0x51; 3..=100 scheduler ticks elapse around the run; no frame leaked; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|ring-3 sleep and yield go through the scheduler

M3.oracle: ring-3 program: channel_create, vmo_create, channel_write of 16 bytes + the VMO handle, channel_read on the peer returns 0x10010 with the bytes intact; the sent handle value is consumed (ERR_BAD_HANDLE), the received one carries VMO rights 0x1f; empty queue ERR_SHOULD_WAIT; double close ERR_BAD_HANDLE; exit code 0x1C (else the failing step); no frame leaked; exit 33

ring-3 program: a READ-only duplicate cannot write (ERR_ACCESS), rights cannot be escalated, a WRITE-only duplicate cannot read, a handle without TRANSFER cannot be sent and stays owned, undefined right bits and sending the channel's own ends are ERR_INVALID; exit 0x2D; exit 33

ring-3 program: after handle_close every call on the value is ERR_BAD_HANDLE; a message queued before the close is still read by the peer, then ERR_PEER_CLOSED both ways; a reused slot carries a new generation (same index, different value); exit 0x3E; exit 33

ring-3 program: 4097 bytes or 5 handles -> ERR_INVALID with nothing queued; exactly 4096 bytes delivered; a 4095-byte buffer -> ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL with the message kept; handle capacity 0 refused the same way, 1 accepted (result 0x10000); exit 0x4F; exit 33

a process exits with two channels, a 64 KiB VMO and messages in transit carrying a VMO handle and a channel end (whose queue carries the VMO's original handle): after exit, live channels/endpoints/vmos/handles are 0 and equal to the values before, PMM free frames and heap live blocks/slab pages equal (after a warm-up run); exit 33

handle table unit test in the test kernel: first values 0x10000/0x10001, a closed value refused (BadHandle), the reused slot yields 0x20000, duplicate with a subset works and the copy lacks the missing right, escalation/undefined bits/handle 0/wrong generation refused, 1024 entries then NoResources, live counts back to the start; exit 33

kernel threads: a reader blocked on an empty channel (read + block_current) is woken by a write within 10 ticks and returns the byte (0x42, one block loop); a wake issued while the reader still sleeps is kept as a token so the reader loops once more instead of hanging (0x43, two loops); dropping the peer wakes a blocked reader with PeerClosed (0xC105ED); object counts and frames equal; exit 33

the embedded ELF64 application `hello` (user/apps, x86_64-unknown-none, libnawah) is loaded into a fresh space and run as a process: trace line user|trace|len=14|text=hello from elf, ping(41) = 42, exit code 7 observed through wait_process; one executable segment, >= 2 segments; no frame leaked; exit 33

13 corruptions of the hello image (bad magic, ELFCLASS32, big-endian, ET_DYN, AArch64 machine, phnum 0, phoff past the file, vaddr outside the window, filesz > memsz, offset past the file, entry outside segments, overlapping segments, truncated to 32 bytes) are each refused with their stable K_E_ELF_* code before anything runs; PMM free frames equal before/after; exit 33

a PT_LOAD marked W+X is refused (K_E_ELF_WX); the valid image's pages carry exactly their segment's permissions (executable pages not writable and not NX, writable pages NX, read-only pages NX and not writable), the stack is RW+NX with an unmapped guard page below, destroy returns every frame; exit 33

virtio-blk (modern PCI, split virtqueue, polling) on the lab's 64 MiB image: device present with capacity 131072 sectors, an 8-sector read of the last 8 sectors returns the harness pattern (sector*7+i)&0xFF with 0 mismatches, a read at the capacity and a 100-byte read are refused (K_E_BLK_RANGE), frames equal; exit 33

block I/O under a process address space (what every file syscall does): the virtio-blk registers are mapped in the kernel's shared MMIO window (0xffffa800_0000_0000.., PML4 slot 336), never at the BAR's own address; with a fresh user space's CR3 active a read of sector 0 and a flush succeed, the sector equals the one read under the kernel CR3 and carries the 55AA boot signature, the space is destroyed and frames balance; exit 33 (regression for CI run 39110182649: the BAR at 0xC0_0000_0000 lay in PML4 slot 1, the user range, and the first open faulted)
required_markers: |ktest|pass|block I/O works under a process address space
|ktest|pass|sectors written before the QEMU restart are intact

M3.oracle: two QEMU runs on the same image: phase 1 (blk_persist_write) writes a tag NAWAH-PERSIST|<build id> plus a pattern to the 8 raw sectors before the pattern tail (131056..131063), flushes and reads them back; phase 2 (blk_persist_read, a fresh boot) finds tag, build id and pattern intact (mismatches=0); both phases exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|sectors written before the QEMU restart are intact

M3.oracle: the kernel's FAT32 mounts the volume tools/fat32.py formatted (128992 clusters of 1 sector) and reads /HELLO.TXT (24 bytes), /PATTERN.BIN (20480 bytes, byte for byte, also from offset 20000) and /DIR/INNER.TXT exactly; the root listing has 4 entries (DIR/, SYSTEM/ with the built applications, HELLO.TXT, PATTERN.BIN); a missing file, a path through a file, a non-8.3 name and reading a directory are refused with K_E_FS_NOT_FOUND / NOT_A_DIRECTORY / BAD_NAME / IS_A_DIRECTORY; exit 33

create /NEW.TXT, write 3000 bytes then append 6 (size 3006 = 6 clusters), read back exactly, a second create is refused (K_E_FS_EXISTS), a file is created and read in /DIR, an overwrite at offset 1000 keeps the size, unlink frees 6 and 1 clusters and the free count returns to its start; afterwards the host's fsck.fat -n and tools/fat32.py check find the image consistent; exit 33

two QEMU runs on the same image: phase 1 creates /PERSIST.TXT with NAWAH-FS-PERSIST|<build id> and syncs; phase 2 (fresh boot) reads it back unchanged; after the runs the host's tools/fat32.py reads the same bytes from the image and fsck.fat -n reports it consistent; both phases exit 33

the file_roundtrip application (libnawah, ABI v1.3) creates /APP.TXT with O_CREATE|O_TRUNCATE, writes two parts, closes, reopens read-only, reads the 39 bytes back, gets 0 at end of file, is refused a write through the read-only handle (ERR_ACCESS), stats the size, seeks to 11 and overwrites 'BY', re-reads, syncs: exit 0x60; no file object, handle or frame outlives the process; afterwards tools/fat32.py reads 'written by BYle_roundtrip: second part\n' from the image and fsck.fat -n is clean; exit 33

the path_invalid application gets the documented error for 20 refusals (missing file, relative path, non-8.3 name, directory, path through a file, empty/undefined flags, missing parent, stat/unlink of missing or directory, empty/NUL/overlong path, kernel pointer, bad handle, channel handle to read) and still reads /hello.txt afterwards: exit 0x61; nothing created; no leak; exit 33

the fd_leak application exits with 44 open file handles (20 opens of /HELLO.TXT + 20 duplicates, 4 created files of 1500 bytes incl. /DIR/LEAK3.TXT): afterwards live files = handles = 0 and all object counts equal their values before, the four files stat at 1500 bytes, free clusters are exactly 12 fewer, frames and process records balance; host checks fsck.fat -n and fat32.py check pass; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|a process exiting with 44 open file handles leaks nothing

M3.oracle: with -smp 4 the boot CPU brings up the three application processors (INIT, SIPI, SIPI, trampoline below 1 MiB): the boot line reports madt_cpus=4 online=4, every CPU runs a thread pinned to it that sees its own index through GS and a distinct local APIC ID, each CPU has taken timer ticks of its own, and frames balance after the cross-CPU joins; exit 33

with -smp 4 one thread per CPU increments a counter behind one IrqSpinLock and an atomic counter 100000 times each, concurrently: both totals are exactly 400000 (no lost update, the lock excludes across CPUs); parallel=1 is informational; exit 33

with -smp 4 a thread on another CPU reads a scratch page (caching the translation), the boot CPU unmaps it (invlpg + shootdown IPI, waiting for the acknowledgement) and maps a different frame; the second read on the other CPU returns the new frame's content, the served-request counter advanced, frames balance; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|a remapped kernel page is seen fresh on another CPU

M4.oracle: the launch application spawns /SYSTEM/ECHO.ELF from the lab volume (process_spawn, ABI v1.4) with a channel endpoint as its bootstrap handle (rdi at entry): the moved endpoint is gone from the caller (ERR_BAD_HANDLE), the echo round trip returns the 16-byte message, object_wait_many sees EXITED and process_status = 16, the caller's endpoint sees PEER_CLOSED; refusals: missing file ERR_NOT_FOUND, /HELLO.TXT (not an ELF) ERR_INVALID, a handle without TRANSFER ERR_ACCESS with the handle still usable; exit 0x70; the kernel logs one spawn line per started process (exactly 1: the refused spawns never start anything); no process record, process object, channel, handle, file or frame survives; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|processes from the volume behaved as the syscall contract v1.4 says

M4.oracle: the waiter application: object_wait_many on an empty channel with a 25-tick timeout returns ERR_TIMED_OUT and clock_ticks shows >= 25 ticks passed (never early; the kernel's own clock agrees); a zero timeout polls (ERR_TIMED_OUT at once); refused: no signal, unknown signal, 0 or 65 entries (ERR_INVALID; 64 is the limit), a VMO (ERR_WRONG_TYPE), a stale handle (ERR_BAD_HANDLE), a handle without WAIT (ERR_ACCESS), entries at an unmapped address (ERR_FAULT); a queued message answers at once with the first asserted index (1 of [b,a]); a closed peer asserts PEER_CLOSED only; the clock is monotonic; exit 0x71 with the measured ticks in the upper bits; nothing leaked; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|object_wait_many times out, polls, refuses bad entries; the clock is monotonic

M4.oracle: the child application: process_status of a running child (blocked in its read) is ERR_SHOULD_WAIT; a 30-tick wait for EXITED times out while it is blocked; after the message, a duplicate of the process handle (WAIT only) sees EXITED, process_status on both handles = 11 (the child's exit code), a zero-timeout wait on the exited process answers at once, the reply is read, the endpoint shows PEER_CLOSED, closed handles answer ERR_BAD_HANDLE; a second child whose process handle is closed right after the spawn still answers and exits (PEER_CLOSED within 500 ticks); exit 0x72; two spawn lines; no process record, process object, channel, handle or frame survives; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|processes from the volume behaved as the syscall contract v1.4 says

M4.oracle: the test kernel starts /SYSTEM/SVCMGR.ELF with a control channel and loads /SYSTEM/SVC-ORD.TXT (A; B after A; C after A,B; all /SYSTEM/SVC.ELF with arg `ready`): LOAD answers `OK 3`; LIST polling ends with all three `ready`; B's first start tick >= A's ready tick and C's >= max(A, B ready); closing the control channel makes the manager exit 0 and the services exit on their closed channels: no process, object or frame remains; exactly 4 spawn lines (manager + 3 services); fsck/fat32.py check pass; exit 33

manifest /SYSTEM/SVC-TMO.TXT: M (arg `mute`, never READY, timeout 50 ticks) and D depending on M: LOAD answers `OK 2`; M becomes `failed` with no ready tick, D stays `blocked` and is never started (2 spawn lines: manager + M), the manager still answers LIST afterwards; after the control channel closes everything exits and nothing remains; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|a silent service fails at its timeout

M4.oracle: manifest /SYSTEM/SVC-RST.TXT: X (arg `crash`, exits 1 at once, on-failure, max 3 restarts, backoff 10): LOAD answers `OK 1`; X ends `given_up` with restarts=3 and exit=1 after 4 starts (5 spawn lines with the manager) spanning >= 70 ticks (backoff 10+20+40); the manager still answers LIST; the clock advanced; nothing remains after the control channel closes; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|a crashing service is restarted with backoff up to its limit, then given up

M4.oracle: kernel unit test of tokens and the authority (auth.md §1–2): every token has a distinct identity; a fresh token has no flags; a copy without WRITE cannot revoke (rights are the handle's); only an Authority object counts as authority (a channel does not); revocation shows through every copy; expiry follows the clock at the expiry tick; one live token while held, none after; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|tokens carry identity, expire by the clock, revoke through every copy; only WRITE revokes

M4.oracle: the auth service (manifest /SYSTEM/SVC-AUTH.TXT) starts after its known-answer self-test (user|trace auth|kat|fails=0|pbkdf2_80000=1) and loads 2 lab users; through CONNECT auth: LOGIN admin with the right password answers OK 1000 1000 15 with a usable token (uid 1000, all permissions, expiry ahead); LOGIN user answers OK 1001 1001 8; a wrong password and an unknown name both answer ERR ACCESS with no token; after 5 consecutive failures on admin the right password answers ERR DELAYED <ticks> while user still logs in; after the delay admin logs in and WHOAMI with the token answers the identity; an unknown request answers ERR BAD_REQUEST; the manager and the service exit cleanly, no frame leaks; host checks: fsck/fat32.py and both lab passwords absent from the raw image; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|login gives a session token, refuses bad credentials, delays after 5 failures

M4.oracle: through CONNECT auth: after LOGIN admin, LOCK with the token answers OK and the token is revoked (WHOAMI with it: ERR ACCESS); UNLOCK with a wrong password: ERR ACCESS; UNLOCK with the right password answers the identity with a new token (different identity, usable) while the old one stays refused; LOGOUT with the new token answers OK and afterwards WHOAMI and UNLOCK with it answer ERR ACCESS with no token; WHOAMI without a handle answers ERR BAD_REQUEST; clean exit, no frame leaks; exit 33
required_markers: |ktest|pass|lock revokes, unlock with the password continues the session, logout ends it

lab.note: Lab credentials (auth.md §3): the users database on the image is derived by tools/project.py with hashlib (independent of nawah-crypto); the passwords never reach the image in the clear (fat32.py absent-raw).
